links.reason: Both set a lover's embrace against heaven (கவானிற் றுஞ்சிற் ... தேவர் பான்மையிற்று), but the epic verse never answers or cites the couplet; the trope is common, so 'develops' overstates.
வெகுண்டனன் ... வதை செய்தனன்: the hero kills a murderer-usurper, but the verse passes no judgement; reading it as the king's weeding of the cruel is imposed, and the epic gains nothing from it.

Line 1-2 give a sowing-and-eating image of deeds in the soul, but the verse only introduces the hell scene; it does not 'qualify' Tirumular's subtle body, and the claim that the other side gains from later hell scenes is vague.
Line 3 நுன் பழம் பகை தவ நூறுவாய் is a blessing that Kattiyangaran's rule ending in 2323 (கட்டியங் காரனென்னும் கலியரசழிந்த) fulfils; the note names both ends correctly.
links.text_issue: 2323 is flagged uncertain in the last line, but the fall of Kattiyangaran is clear.

links.reason: Verse 58 is a hard, flagged verse that most likely praises a court bound to the king's hint; nothing in it laments lack of correction, and Kural 447 (இடிக்குந் துணையாரை) makes no incompatible claim.
This is story order: 2327 has him enter the old city (மூதூர்) worshipped, 2524 a street procession; the 'private return becomes state procession' and 'same city' are not in either Tamil.

1613 follows 1609 in plot (மாதவன் ... பொழிலின் மறைந்தான் / துகில் பற்றுபு கொணர்ந்தார்); the 'who has power in the household' lesson is not stated in either verse, and the queen as speaker of 1613 is inferred.

Line 2 'அரசன் ஒன்றோ இருபிறப்பாளன்' infers high birth from skill, which does cut against 409's learning over birth; but the Kural does not deny that skill can mark birth, so 'explicitly denies' overstates and the clash is mild.

1383 only shows the girl fainting (மின்னென மின்னிலம் எய்தினள்); birds, lamps and eyes are not in it, so 'only here does the epic count its cost' is untrue, and the patikam link is just summary and detail.

Neelakesi says the Veda is made (செய்கையும் புதுமையும்) and joined with killing (கொலை ... தீக்கதிச் செலுத்தும்); Tirumular says no dharma lacks the Veda and the wise left argument (தர்க்க வாதத்தை விட்டு) and recited it. The claims on the Veda are incompatible.
21 gives only a childless king worshipping a sage (இல்லையென்று எவ்வம் கூர்ந்து); the sister's son and renunciation are not in the verse, and Kural 61's அறிவறிந்த மக்கட்பேறு is not tested by it.

3092 names the cutting of four காதி and knowing the three times; Kural 9's எண்குணத்தான் is not named, so calling them 'the same figure counted two ways' is assumed, and the verse does not qualify the couplet.
links.text_issue: Marked reading of 3092 trails off; line 2 நான்மைவரம்பாகி uncertain.

links.reason: 1766 proclaims ten days (ஈரைஞ் ஞாள்), 1768 shows kings and அரசரல்லாரும் surrounding the city; this is plot sequence and the 'crowd outruns kings' point is slight.

123 shows the king restraining his sword (கரத்து வாளும் ... விலக்கி); 172 the bird pecking eyes. No incompatible claim is made, and 'patience is a trait of the body not the soul' is nowhere in the Tamil.

Both have the friend point the hill-man to the waterfall village (அருவிசூடிய உயர்வரை எம்ஊர் / தூஅருவி ... பாக்கம் இது எம் இடம்); AA 12 is not a fulfilment of AN 38 but another poem using the same convention, so 'develops' misfits.

The queen says she will go to her own palace (என்றாள்) and the king lays his crown at her feet; she is leaving, not salting a quarrel in measure, and the verse says nothing of timing, so the Kural's measure is not 'kept'.

272 names mantra-truth, austerity, or just rule as ways to Indra's world and gives no verdict on grace; Tirumanthiram 1006 gives worship as one way. Neither excludes the other, so there is no tension.

Both have the friend use the elephant that strips the யா tree (யாஅத்து ... உருவக் குத்தி / யாஅம் ஒற்றி), one for a herd and one for a mate; the pair truly shows the image turned two ways, but 'qualifies' is the wrong type.

72 reports a view that the dead are not reborn and there are no two deeds (இறந்தனர் பிறந்ததில்லை); 49 only says the soul is other than the body. The dismissal answers in 73, not on 49, so 'rests on 49' overreaches.

Both use the door of நிறை: 714 அருநிறைக் கதவம் நீக்கி ... நெஞ்சம் என்னும் கன்னிமாடம் புகுந்து, Kural 1251 நிறையென்னும் கதவு; the epic changes the breaker and ends in a marriage vow, which is specific and true.

Both show a king on elephants under the white umbrella fallen (கொலையானை ... குளிர்வெண் குடைக்கீழ் / யானை ... குடைநிழற்கீழ்); but 1464 has no named king or battle and no cause of deeds, so the gains claims are not in the verse.

Both use a sea to cross with a raft (துயர்க் கடலை நீந்தும் புணை / பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல் நீந்துவர்); but the epic sea is sorrow, and the Kural has no raft or human aid, so 'qualifies' and the gain to the couplet do not hold.
Soolamani 1902 shows the king bowing crown to ground (மணிமுடி நிலமுற வணங்கி); this only illustrates Kural 9's bowing, and the 'cost of pride' is not stated in the Tamil.

The hymn says by love the eight karmas pass and by that love they do not (காதலால் ... கழிப / ... கழியா); this affirms and limits Kural 350, so it is a qualification not a pure tension, and 'denies what the couplet affirms' is untrue.
links.text_issue: Verse flagged uncertain: காதல் and மறைதி open.

links.reason: 3074 gives ஞானம், உயிரோம்பல், கருணை, சீலம் as army; faith (காட்சி) is absent, so it is not the three jewels of 2845, and 'what the three do' is not shown.

67 has scattered girdles that nobody wants (கொள்ளும் நீரர் இன்மையின்), 2662 has defeated women giving girdles to the king; only the word for girdles (கலை) is shared and the 'changed ownership' lesson is invented.
1437 follows 1436 in plot (கேட்டே ... வீட்டுநன் னெறியைப் பெற்றார்); the ascetics' conversion answers the teaching, but this is mostly sequence and the 'settles the debate' reading is the marker's.

Both change a bride's ear-ornaments (தோடு, குழை, கடிப்பு); but 2440 swaps plain for gems and 488 swaps gold and gems for a small simple adornment, so 'same step in the same words' misdescribes the direction.
Both are ordinary dress verses with a gem girdle (மணிமேகலை); that the girl 'repeats her mother's dressing' and the game is a step to marriage is not in either Tamil.

899 has a vow of waiting until he worships her feet (தோற்று வந்து சிலம்படி கைதொழ), which is pique not the loss of மானம் of Kural 969; the vow as 'measure of honour' is not stated and the verse is flagged uncertain.
links.text_issue: நோற்பன் நோற்றனை நீ hard to divide.

links.reason: Both have Death and a net (கூற்றுவன் ... வலையை வைத்தான் / கூற்றம் ... வலையகத்து); the epic's 'தேற்றாம்' still admits ignorance of the way out, so 'folly becomes failure of will' is a generous reading.
594 says energy draws wealth; 371 says fate (ஆகூழ்) produces steadfastness. Fate then energy then wealth is a chain, not a reversal, so 'reverses' is untrue; 371 qualifies 594, a within-Kural link.
1784 is the next event in plot (அயோத்தியாள் வேந்தன் புக்கான்) after the call of 1783; 'the roll-call is the proclamation's result' is plot order, not a link.

The only tie is the word சுணங்கன்; Tirumanthiram 533 is dogs for those who grieve the guru, while 960 is an alchemical simile for rebirth by a deathbed mantra, so the 'mantra decides birth both ways' pairing and its gains are stretched.
Kural 57 puts the best guard in a woman's own நிறை; Civakan says women are உண்ணிறை உடைய அல்ல. The shared word நிறை fixes a real opposed claim, with the epic noting its own occasion for it.
199 has deeds breeding deeds (சூழ்வினை ... வீழ்வினை பிறிதும் ஆக்கி) but no seed image, so 'both see rebirth as a growing seed' is wrong for 199; Tirumanthiram 120 is also flagged uncertain.
707 turns the insult back (வேந்தன் பேயிற் பேசிய பிள்ளையே ஆக) on the king who in 703 called him a child; this is a reply, not a tension of claims.
1713 has only a drum like the sea of the end of an age (ஊழிநீர்); wedding-turned-funeral drums of Naladiyar 23 are not there and the note admits the poem does not say it.
1630 gives the ruse hinted at in 1629 (ஓர் உபாயத்தால் ஒளிக்கலுற்றான்): ஓர் விஞ்சை தாழிருள் எழினி; this clarifies a detail in plot order and the 'joins the game unseen' lesson is thin.
40 puts ninety-six men inside the machine (தொண்ணூற் றறுவரை மறையும்); 49 shows them bursting out (போர்ப்படை ஆனதே). A trap and its springing, but the note restates the plot and 49 is flagged uncertain.
1992 grades gifts by receiver, giver and gift (உலைவி லேற்போன்); it names no worship test and Tirumanthiram 508 gives one for the receiver, so they do not give opposed answers.

2082 makes wealth a goddess who leaves men and seeks new ones (புதிய காமுறும்); Kural 332 compares it to a crowd breaking up. Fleeting wealth is shared; the personified will is the real difference, but the pair is mostly a shared theme.
2958 only recalls the snake-bite cure; 1285 shows Civakan promising she will not die, not the cure, and the 'leaving takes the life back' lesson is not in the Tamil.
